intro: A noisy sequence can violate a known increasing trend. Pool adjacent violations to find the closest nondecreasing fit under weighted squared error.
task: Return the nondecreasing vector minimizing sum(weights*(fitted-values)**2) with the original observation order fixed.
requirements: values and weights are equal-length vectors. Every weight lies in [1e-8,1e6].
Use adjacent blocks: start with one observation per block, and merge neighboring blocks whenever the left weighted mean is greater than the right weighted mean.
Assign each observation its final block mean. Do not sort values or their positions; equality between adjacent fitted values is allowed.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Keep a stack of contiguous blocks with their weight sums and weighted-value sums.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: After merging the last two blocks, compare the new block with its predecessor again; a violation can cascade backward.

explanation: When two adjacent block means decrease, their unconstrained estimates violate monotonicity. Combining them at their joint weighted mean is the least-squares compromise for that pooled block.
A merge may create a new violation with the preceding block, so checking backward is essential. Sorting the observations would solve a different problem and discard their original order.
